narrative: Material PL1__M26EDEC5 shows smooth, normally distributed daily demand averaging 1,188 units with no detectable trend. Lead times exhibit moderate variability (CV=0.567) ranging from 0.44 to 5.97 working days, making lead-time variance the dominant stockout risk driver at 93% of total sigma_LTD. The (r,Q) continuous-review policy with an EOQ-derived order quantity of 13,517 units and safety stock of 2,592 units is recommended to achieve the 95% service level target while remaining within the 17,779-unit storage capacity constraint.

research_insights.selection_rationale: Smooth demand with normal distribution and non-intermittent consumption (100% non-zero days) makes the classical (r,Q) EOQ-based policy optimal. Continuous review is appropriate given daily demand visibility and the need to respond to lead-time variability.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage capacity of 17,779 units is not binding (SS+Q=16,109). If demand grows by >10%, the capacity buffer narrows and may require renegotiation of storage allocation.
